title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X/S is smooth of relative dimension 1 in characteristic p, with relative Frobenius F: X -> X^{(p)}. Write Z = X^{(p)}; on this page Z is presented as the ringed space (X^p, Λ), where Λ is the sheaf of p-th powers, i.e. O_{X^{(p)}} viewed inside O_X.

The objects:
- F_*O_X is locally free of rank p over Λ. A local p-basis x (a relative coordinate) gives the basis 1, x, ..., x^{p-1}.
- Q is the quotient F_*O_X / O_{X^{(p)}}, locally free of rank p-1 with basis ẋ, ẋ^2, ..., ẋ^{p-1}. Hence det Q ≅ det F_*O_X.
- The previous page constructed, via the duality between F_*O_X and its dual twisted by ω (the trace/Cartier duality), a canonical isomorphism (**): det(Q)^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S}^{⊗(p-1)} ⊗ Λ.
- For p = 2 this says Ω^1_{X^{(2)}/S} is canonically a square, with Q itself as the square root (a Frobenius theta characteristic). He raises the pointless conic (Serre–Tate–Fröhlich) as a possible obstruction.
- For p odd he wants to refine (**) to a canonical square root ψ: det Q ≅ Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S}^{⊗(p-1)/2}. He computes that, in the basis given by a p-basis x, (**) sends (ẋ∧ẋ^2∧…∧ẋ^{p-1})^{⊗2} to Δ·(dx̃)^{⊗(p-1)}. Here Δ = ±(p-1)! is a universal constant, ±1 by Wilson's theorem.

This page.
1. The boxed formula (***) defines Ψ locally by Ψ(ẋ∧ẋ^2∧…∧ẋ^{p-1}) = (dx̃)^{⊗(p-1)/2} ⊗ 1_Λ, where x̃ = x^{(p)} = 1⊗x on X^{(p)}. Up to the universal constant Δ, its square is (**).
2. One must show Ψ does not depend on the p-basis. He first tries a direct computation: write y = Σ a_i x^i with a_i ∈ Λ, so dy = f'(x)dx with f'(x) a unit. This is crossed out.
3. He replaces it with a rigidity argument:
   - For two p-bases x and y, Ψ_y / Ψ_x is a unit whose square is 1, because both square to the canonical (**) times the same Δ.
   - So it is a section of μ_2. Since p is odd, μ_2 is the étale double cover (Z/2)_Z.
   - The p-bases form a scheme P over Z, which carries a morphism P -> (Z/2)_Z.
   - P has connected fibres (an open subscheme of affine space of polynomial coefficients), so the morphism is constant fibrewise. It equals +1 on the diagonal x = y.
   - Hence Ψ is canonical, and also functorial ('sa variance').
4. Programme notes:
   - (a) Application: a global cohomological definition for X/S proper smooth of relative dimension 1. The next page sets up the self-dual diagram relating the Hodge and conjugate filtrations on H^1_DR, Frobenius F and Cartier C, transposes of each other up to sign.
   - (b) Question: generalise these determinant relations to higher dimension.

Modern statement: for a smooth curve in odd characteristic there is a canonical isomorphism det(F_*O_X) ≅ ω_{X^{(p)}}^{⊗(p-1)/2}, normalised by the monomial basis of a coordinate. It is a canonical square root of the duality isomorphism det(F_*O_X)^{⊗2} ≅ ω^{⊗(p-1)}.
errors: The sign of Δ is unclear across the two pages. (-1)^{(p-1)-1}·(p-1)! with p odd equals (-1)·(-1) = +1 by Wilson's theorem, yet the previous page concludes Δ = -1. The exponent as transcribed may be wrong, or the sign convention in (**) differs. Either way Δ is a universal constant in {±1}, so the rigidity argument (a ratio in μ_2, normalised at x = y) is unaffected. Only the precise compatibility Ψ^{⊗2} = ±(**) needs fixing.

The connectedness of the fibres of the scheme P of p-bases is asserted, not proved. Locally P is an open subscheme (the derivative is a unit) of an affine space of coefficients, so the claim is plausible. One also needs P -> Z to be faithfully flat or to have local sections for 'constant fibrewise' to give 'equal to 1'.

The direct computation via the change of p-base is abandoned, so there is no explicit verification that the transition determinant equals N(f')^{(p-1)/2}. This is acceptable given the rigidity argument.

ideas.what: Canonical square root of the Frobenius discriminant isomorphism: det(F_*O_X) (equivalently det of F_*O_X/O) ≅ ω^{⊗(p-1)/2} for curves in odd characteristic, normalised by Ψ(ẋ∧…∧ẋ^{p-1}) = (dx̃)^{⊗(p-1)/2}.
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of Frobenius direct image, det F_*O_X ≅ ω^{(p-1)/2}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud (1982, sheaf B = F_*O/O on curves); X. Sun (2008, 'Direct images of bundles under Frobenius morphism'), det F_*W ≅ det W ⊗ ω^{(p-1)rk W/2}; Joshi–Ramanan–Xia–Yu for curves

ideas.what: Rigidity argument: two candidate isomorphisms with the same square differ by a μ_2-valued function on the scheme of p-bases (coordinates); connected fibres force it to be constant, hence independent of choice.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / torsor-of-coordinates (Gelfand–Kazhdan style) argument for canonicity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; formal-coordinates torsor in Beilinson–Drinfeld style

ideas.what: Case p = 2: Ω^1_{X^{(2)}/S} is canonically a square, with Q = F_*O/O as square root (a canonical theta characteristic), together with the question of the pointless conic.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical theta characteristic B = F_*O_X/O_X in characteristic 2

ideas.what: Plan for a global cohomological version (proper smooth curves) and for a generalisation of the determinant relations to higher dimension.
ideas.modern_name: det F_*O_X ≅ ω^{p^{n-1}(p-1)/2}-type formulas in dimension n
ideas.usually_credited_to: X. Sun (2008) and later work on Frobenius direct images

missed.claim: A canonical (sign-fixed, coordinate-normalised) isomorphism det(F_*O_X/O) ≅ Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S}^{⊗(p-1)/2} for relative curves in odd characteristic, over a general base S. It is proved by a μ_2-rigidity argument on the scheme of p-bases, decades before the published (mostly non-canonical, over a field) formulas.
missed.quote: Ψ(ẋ∧ẋ^2∧…∧ẋ^{p-1}) = dx̃^{⊗(p-1)/2}⊗1_Λ … P sur Z est à fibres connexes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The literature usually states det F_*O_X ≅ ω^{(p-1)/2} up to non-canonical isomorphism, via Riemann–Roch or degree computations. A canonical relative version with explicit normalisation is useful in families: for Frobenius-twisted determinant line bundles on moduli of curves and for the sign conventions linking Frobenius and Cartier duality.

missed.claim: He asks to generalise the canonical determinant relations (the p = 2 canonical square-root statement and the odd-p square root) to higher relative dimension. He also plans a global cohomological interpretation for proper smooth curves.
missed.quote: ? Généralisation des relations précédentes à la dim. supérieure ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical (not merely abstract) isomorphisms det F_*O_X ≅ ω^{N} in higher dimension, with explicit signs, are not standard. They bear on Frobenius-split varieties and on the determinant of the de Rham–Witt / Cartier structures.

deep.surprise_reason: An early (c. 1972) canonical, base-general form of det F_*O_X ≅ ω^{(p-1)/2} for curves, with a neat rigidity proof. The underlying fact is now known (Raynaud, Sun), so it is a notable unpublished detail but not a major missing result.
transcription_corrections: Λ here denotes the sheaf of p-th powers (O_{X^{(p)}} inside O_X); compare 'Z=(X^p,Λ)' and '(a_i ∈ Λ)'. It is not a separate line bundle.
'on veut donc que ce morphisme est constant' should probably read 'on voit donc que ce morphisme est constant fibre à fibre, ce qui donne ce qu'on veut'.
'Ce qui donne une version [?] directe' is likely 'une version plus directe'.
'Avec dim rel. 1' line: likely 'Application: la définition cohomologique globale (X lisse propre sur S de dim rel. 1)'.
The crossed-out condition '…∈ B^*' plausibly refers to units (of the coordinate ring), i.e. the derivative of the change of p-base is invertible.
